data.title: Thread
data.tagline: A thread is an execution path inside a process, and threads in one process usually share memory and resources.
data.learningOutcome: You can identify threads in one process, determine whether they share memory, and ask for synchronization evidence during concurrent updates.
data.description: A service process can use several threads for concurrent requests. Threads A and B can both access the same cache; sharing helps communication but can cause overwrites and races. A thread is not an independent process with fully isolated memory, and actual parallelism depends on the runtime and workload.

learning.assumes: You know one process can keep handling multiple requests.
learning.outcome: You can identify threads in one process, determine whether they share memory, and ask for synchronization evidence during concurrent updates.

distinctions.label: Process
distinctions.explanation: A Thread exists inside a process and shares its address space; a Process is an isolated execution environment with separate memory and PID.

distinctions.label: Coroutine
distinctions.explanation: A Thread is preemptively scheduled by the OS kernel; a Coroutine is cooperatively scheduled in user space.

explanation.title: Problem and key mechanism
explanation.text: When two threads in one process read and write a shared cache at the same time, a later write can overwrite an earlier result; after confirming the shared object and thread relationship, use a lock, queue, or immutable result to order writes and record observable state.

explanation.title: Verify stable shared results
explanation.text: Repeated concurrent runs should keep the correct final value. Threads still share the process failure and memory boundary.

explanation.title: Video export also uses shared threads
explanation.text: When a video exporter processes segments on multiple threads, they share one progress counter. Updates must be synchronized to prevent regressions or missed progress.

data.boundary: A thread belongs inside a process and usually shares its memory; it is not an isolated process. Parallel behavior and suitability for CPU or I/O work depend on the runtime and scheduler.

lessonPractice.title: Thread A and B belong to one process and update a shared cache concurrently. What should you verify first?

options.label: Verify that shared reads and writes use a lock, queue, or another synchronization rule
options.feedback: Correct. Threads in one process share memory, so concurrent mutation needs an explicit order and evidence.

options.label: Verify that each thread has a different process ID and fully isolated memory
options.feedback: Threads in one process normally share its memory and process identity.

options.label: Add more threads so extra concurrency automatically removes overwrites
options.feedback: More competitors do not create synchronization and can increase conflicts.

data.agentPrompt: Identify which threads belong to the same process and which state they share. Add an appropriate synchronization boundary around shared-cache writes and record process ID, thread ID, and final value. Run two threads concurrently several times and verify no update is lost.
